record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: For a group G and any matrix A in M_{r,s}(ZG), is the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of the right-multiplication operator r_A: N(G)^r → N(G)^s always at least 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1 (Determinant Conjecture for a group G). For any matrix A ∈ Mr,s(ZG), the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of the N (G)-homomorphism rA : N (G)r → N (G)s given by right multiplication with A satisfies detN(G) (rA) ≥ 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a discrete group, and let $\mathbb{Z}G$ denote its integral group ring. Let $\mathcal{N}(G)$ denote the group von Neumann algebra of $G$, equipped with its canonical finite normal trace $\mathrm{tr}_{\mathcal{N}(G)}$. For $r,s \geq 1$ and a matrix $A \in M_{r,s}(\mathbb{Z}G)$, consider the bounded $\mathcal{N}(G)$-linear operator
$$r_A : \mathcal{N}(G)^r \longrightarrow \mathcal{N}(G)^s$$
given by right multiplication by $A$. The Fuglede–Kadison determinant $\det_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(r_A) \in [0,\infty)$ is defined by
$$\det_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(r_A) \;=\; \exp\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\int_{0^+}^{\infty} \log(\lambda)\, d\mu_{|r_A|}(\lambda)\right),$$
where $\mu_{|r_A|}$ is the spectral measure of $|r_A| = \sqrt{r_A^* r_A}$ with respect to the trace on $M_r(\mathcal{N}(G))$ (with the convention that the integral over the positive part is taken, and $\det_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(r_A) := 1$ if the kernel suffices to make the integral $-\infty$, in which case one sets the determinant to be the exponential of the regularized integral).

Prove or disprove: for every discrete group $G$ and every matrix $A \in M_{r,s}(\mathbb{Z}G)$,
$$\det_{\mathcal{N}(G)}(r_A) \;\geq\; 1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Determinant Conjecture is known to hold for a large class of groups, most notably all sofic groups (a theorem of Elek–Szabó), and various extensions (e.g., to certain invariant random subgroup settings). However, it remains open for arbitrary discrete groups; in particular, no proof is known for non-sofic groups, and the existence of non-sofic groups is itself open.

status_evidence.title: Invariant Random Subgroups, Soficity, and Lück's determinant conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: For every free group, there exists an IRS satisfying the determinant conjecture that is not co-sofic, suggesting the determinant conjecture may be weaker than soficity.
status_evidence.claim: The Determinant Conjecture is known for sofic groups (Elek–Szabó) and is conjectured for all groups, but remains open beyond sofic groups.

status_evidence.title: Fuglede–Kadison Determinants and Sofic Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Connects Fuglede-Kadison determinants to sofic entropy of algebraic actions; relies on the determinant conjecture being known for sofic groups.
status_evidence.claim: Determinant conjecture established for sofic groups.
